Cleveland can likely tack on 15 more pounds without seeing an ounce of drop-off in his athleticism. Already a plus runner with a solid-average throwing arm, the future is bright for Cleveland so long as the hit tool catches up with the raw ability.

Tralongo can really hit, and he's done so on just about every stage. He's got a short-compact swing that can push and pull the ball. His willingness to use the right-center field gap is well-documented. Tralongo has average power, but doesn't project to be a homerun hitter at the next level. His polish and approach are his best offensive tools. Tralongo moves well side-to-side and has a shot to play second base moving forward, though some believe he's best suited for third base where his average speed might operate most efficiently. He possesses an average arm.

Champion is a high-pedigree competitor with a long, decorated track record, as well as representing his country for Team USA. He'll run it up to 92, living in the upper 80s as the game goes on. He's got tremendous feel for his secondaries; an upper 70s curveball and a changeup in the same velocity bucket. Champion will mix it up and go heavy toward his weapons as the game goes on. He doesn't have a carrying pitch yet, though some believe the changeup to be a potential above average weapon going forward. He's got a starter profile, holding velocity deep into games, posting large pitch counts when given the opportunity. Champion has been well known in scouting circles going back to his early, early teenage years. He's been in the trenches for quite some time.

Gregor's athleticism immediately sticks out when watching him throw multiple innings. It's a high leg-kick and a fast-moving operation that he repeats well and does so with ease. Gregor is a ground ball machine with a sinker that's been up to 96 with steep angle and arm-side run. He'll tumble over a mid-80s changeup at times to lefties, but it's his 2600-rpm slider that short, two-plane life that gets whiffs. Gregor doesn't project a strikeout artist at the next level, but has the look of an innings-eater and soft-contact machine that could handle multiple roles.

Frankel is a polished righty with a four-pitch mix and a fastball already flirting with mid-90s velocity. His best secondary is a sharp slider in the low-80s with late, diving life. He's messed around with altering his grips a bit to achieve a more conventional curveball to supplement the slider, though it's a work in progress. Frankel also throws a changeup that has been hit-or-miss in his outings, but has flashed some feel for turning them over and generating some shape in-game.

Frankel began his career at Liberty where he strung together two strong seasons before taking his game to Tulane for his draft-eligible 2026 campaign.

Hersh is a physical bat with a broad, imposing frame. He stays well-connected in his swing, making tight turns around the baseball showing off his above average raw power in games against some of the better arms South Florida has to offer. Hersh has some tools behind the plate including sneaky athleticism and above average arm strength. Scouts have said they'd like to see a greater emphasis in getting into a deeper squat to improve overall receiving skills, but that can come with training. Hersh is a draft-eligible sophomore.

Chicoli a a strong, high-waisted righty with long levers and plenty of physical projection remaining. He presently works up to 93, living 90-92 with arm-side run, emphasizing glove-side command. Chicoli throws a mid-70s curveball with good depth, but it's his low-80s changeup that has scouts talking. He sells the offspeed with real conviction and pronates hard, turning the pitch over with serious parachute. Chicoli generates considerable fade on the pitch and solid depth off his fastball tunnel. He features a longer arm action with a wide elbow spiral, not too dissimilar from someone like George Kirby. He'll need to prove he can spin the baseball.

Rogers is a standout behind the plate with explosion out of the crouch and arm strength that really projects going forward. He showcases a lightning quick transfer and should be one of the better controllers of the run game in this class. He's a sturdy-built backstop with weight well distributed throughout his frame. Scouts would like to see him keep the ball in front of him with a bit more consistency, but he's more than strong enough an athlete to get there. He should be able to hold onto his athleticism longer than most. Something like a Yan Gomes body. Rogers swings a heavy barrel and leverages hard to his pull-side. It's power-over-hit right now but scouts like the upside of the bat.

Musci is an explosive right-handed arm with a ton of deception coming out of his drop-and-drive operation. He hides the ball well, and that really plays as his low-to-mid 90s fastball possesses legit carry through the zone, and a reasonably flat approach angle too. The slider and changeup lag a little bit behind his dynamic fastball, and there may be some reliever risk here considering the effort and unorthodox delivery, but there's plenty of pro traits here.

Swygart is an interesting left-handed slugger with easy bat speed, some rhythm at the plate and a feel for his pull-side. He features loose hips, feel for the barrel and quick hands at the plate that allow his strength to play to all-fields. He's pull-happy at this stage, but his bat speed should translate against more premium pitching at the next level. He's a balanced hitter with obvious slugging upside.

DePaolo is an ultra-intense competitor with a violent approach at the plate and a consistent intent to do damage offensively. His plate appearances are unnerving for the opposing pitcher as he sets the tone with max-effort practice swings between pitches. DePaolo has some skills with the bat featuring some hitterish tendencies and a pull-side emphasis. The bat speed is clear, though he sometimes throttles it down in the box in an effort to time up good pitching. DePaolo is a soldier behind the plate, sacrificing the body and blocking most everything that bounces in front of him. He's got an average arm, but is explosive out of the crouch. DePaolo has a shot to stick behind the plate moving forward. He is also an average runner. He is a draft-eligible sophomore

Newstrom is a physically-mature offensive powerhouse with game power and the ability to impact the game with his arm. Scouts are split on whether he'll end up too "boxy" to play catcher, but he'll have a permanent home at third base if that's the case.

Turner is a twitchy hitter in the box with fast hips, quick hands and ringing power. The foot speed and instincts here are above his peers; a quick step out of the box and on the bases. He's an anxious runner who consistently looks to take a free base with his above average speed and coachability with in-game adjustments. Turner is extremely strong with a stacked, explosive lower half. His broad shoulders and advanced frame point toward above average game power upside. Turner also has a solid average arm that projects to get stronger as his upper-body catches up with his lower-half. The whole profile works in right field. Some Marcell Ozuna comparisons here.
